sentiment.rationale: The document shows genuine operational momentum: revenue up 18% YoY, core loss per share improved from ($1.13) to ($0.49), free cash flow usage improved from ($3.9B) to ($2.3B), and management describes a 'really solid quarter' with a 'recovery plan in full swing.' However, full-year free cash flow guidance was not formally raised (management said 'we're not going to adjust that full year range right now'), and a structural risk was disclosed: approximately 50 China deliveries are at risk due to tariffs, with customers indicating they will not take delivery. The positive operational trajectory is partially offset by this unresolved tariff risk, resulting in a moderately positive score.

summary.revenue: $19.5 billion, up 18% from $16.6 billion in 1Q24, primarily reflecting higher commercial delivery volume.
summary.eps: GAAP loss per share of ($0.16) and core (non-GAAP) loss per share of ($0.49), improved from ($0.56) and ($1.13) respectively in 1Q24.
summary.guidance: Full-year free cash flow guidance not adjusted; management expects 2H free cash flow to turn positive and accelerate as the year exits. 737 production expected to reach 38 per month over the next few months, with a request to increase to 42 per month later this year. 787 production expected to increase to 7 per month over the next few months. 777X first delivery still anticipated in 2026. Approximately 50 China deliveries in plan for the balance of the year, but customers have indicated they will not take delivery due to tariffs.
summary.margin: GAAP operating margin 2.4% (vs. (0.5)% in 1Q24); core (non-GAAP) operating margin 1.0% (vs. (2.3)% in 1Q24). Commercial Airplanes operating margin (6.6)% (vs. (24.6)% in 1Q24). Defense, Space & Security operating margin 2.5% (vs. 2.2% in 1Q24). Global Services operating margin 18.6% (vs. 18.2% in 1Q24).
key_risks: Approximately 50 China deliveries at risk due to tariffs; customers in China have indicated they will not take delivery.
Input tariffs on components from Japan and Italy (10% tariff) affecting wide-body airplane costs; net annual impact less than $500 million.
Potential retaliatory tariffs from other countries could affect ability to deliver aircraft.
Seat certification issues affecting some 787 deliveries expected to be a challenge for the balance of the year.
SPS (Jenkintown) fire impacting fastener supply; team scrambling to find alternate sources.
Structural risk: ongoing certification programs for 737-7, 737-10, and 777X with no change to previously shared timelines.
Pending acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems (closing expected around midyear) subject to regulatory approval and customary conditions.
key_opportunities: F-47 win: selected by U.S. Air Force to design, build and deliver next-generation fighter aircraft, securing fighter franchise for decades.
Digital Aviation Solutions divestiture for $10.55 billion (all cash, net proceeds ~$10 billion) strengthens balance sheet.
Strong demand environment: total company backlog grew to $545 billion, including over 5,600 commercial airplanes; key programs sold out into next decade.
737 production ramp: currently in low 30s per month, expected to reach 38 per month, with potential to increase to 42 per month later this year.
787 production ramp: currently at 5 per month, expected to increase to 7 per month; shadow factory closed, rework completed.
Defense, Space & Security stabilizing: EACs held for the quarter, T-7 achieved first two incentive milestones, MQ-25 began final assembly.
Global Services continued strong performance with 18.6% operating margin and $5 billion in orders.
Portfolio streamlining: additional smaller divestitures being considered to focus on core businesses.
